title: The Wild Ass and the Flattering Jackal

keywords: the wild ass and the jackal
full_text:
In a secluded desert valley, a wild ass grazed peacefully upon wild thyme and mountain grass, fleet of foot and independent of any master. In the rocky hills nearby dwelt an aging, wounded lion who could no longer run down game, accompanied by a sycophantic jackal who scavenged his scraps.

The hungry lion growled: 'Jackal! Go into the valley and lure the fat wild ass into my gorge, or I shall devour you!'

The jackal trotted down into the valley, put on an expression of fawning reverence, and called out: 'Greetings, noble monarch of the steppes! Our sovereign the lion has grown old and weary of hunting. He has observed your magnificent speed and stately bearing, and desires to proclaim you the King of all the Grazing Beasts! Come with me to his cave to receive the royal diadem.'

The wild ass, though simple, was not devoid of common sense. He stopped grazing, tilted his long ears, and looked at the jackal with sharp, skeptical eyes.

'O jackal,' said the wild ass, 'your tongue is sweet as wild honey, but your tracks smell of the slaughterhouse! Since when does the lion crown kings among the creatures he was born to devour? If he wishes to honor me, let him send his crown down with the mountain breeze; my throat prefers the wild grass of the valley to the coronation feasts of a predator’s cave.'

The wild ass kicked up his heels, snorted at the scheming scavenger, and galloped across the open desert, outstripping all pursuit.

The frustrated jackal returned empty-handed to the roaring lion, while the wild ass lived in freedom, proving that healthy skepticism preserves life against the sweetest flatteries.
moral: Do not listen to the flattering counsel of a predator who seeks to lure you into his master's claws.
